lesson: Feed an underground-belt entrance straight from behind, never from the side: a side-fed entrance blocks one lane. A turn with no belt behind it is a curve that keeps lanes, so it won't move items to the other lane.

lesson: In belt-routing puzzles, list each row's segment-order constraints first; break ordering cycles by sending one item around via a free outer lane, using the inserter-fed start tile and the end tile as vertical underground entrance/exit.
context: ops: @serf Transport Belt Madness, level 2 of 5, on this island. 8 input chests each need a belt to the output chest with the same item. Belt starts and ends: iron-plate: [gps=-4.5,-2.5] to [gps=5.5,2.5]; copper-plate: [gps=-4.5,-1.5] to [gps=5.5,3.5]; steel-plate: [gps=-4.5,-0.5] to [gps=5.5,-2.5]; copper-ore: [gps=-4.5,0.5] to [gps=5.5,4.5]; iron-ore: [gps=-4.5,2.5] to [gps=5.5,-1.5]; coal: [gps=-4.5,3.5] to [gps=5.5,5.5]; wood: [gps=-4.5,4.5] to [gps=5.5,0.5]; iron-gear-wheel: [gps=-4.5,5.5] to [gps=5.5,-0.5].
